R01.note: Solid idempotency, guarded update, outbox and DLQ, but insufficient stock just rolls back/DLQs, no visibility timeout, no structured logs with ids and no reconciliation.

R02.note: Strong and complete, but the reservation is keyed unique on order_id alone (not order_id+sku), versioned schemas are deferred and there is no graceful shutdown or prefetch bound.

R03.note: Good dedupe and guarded update, but no stock CHECK, outbox/separate sender is vague, insufficient stock is ambiguously not acked, tests miss crash and email-failure cases, no reconciliation.

R04.note: Dedupe is a check-and-record without a stated unique constraint, no provider idempotency key, no permanent-failure classification, thin out-of-stock path, and reconciliation checks stock drift rather than paid orders vs emails.

R05.note: Thorough and correct on the core items; lacks versioned schema/cancel ordering, graceful shutdown and prefetch, and has no periodic reconciliation job.

R06.note: Strong core design with out-of-order handling, but no explicit schema validation, no graceful shutdown or prefetch bound, and no reconciliation job.

R07.note: Good design with reconciliation and graceful shutdown, but no provider idempotency key, no transient-vs-permanent classification and no payload schema validation.

R08.note: Correct core consumer and outbox, but does not explain why a commit-then-crash is safe, ignores event ordering, no visibility timeout, and lacks reconciliation and retention.

R09.note: Complete and correct on idempotency, outbox, failures and tests; missing out-of-order/cancel handling, visibility timeout and a reconciliation job.

R10.note: Correct core with a clear backorder path and good tests; no out-of-order handling, no visibility timeout or graceful shutdown, and no reconciliation.
